gap: The Sort pill is the weakest control in the pane. Its label is regular weight and lighter grey, where A's is semibold and darker, and its fill is #F6F6F6 against A's #F9F9F9. Against the #FCFCFC List it looks disabled rather than like a control you can click.
gapTheirs: The List header band is not the List's ground. Down the column at x=700 it goes from #FCFCFC to #F6F6F6 and #FAFAFA, with hairlines at y≈31 and y≈72, where the rows sit on flat #FCFCFC. Each row's file icon is a shaded paper sheet about 30 px tall, drawn in blurred #DDD lines. Both add grey-on-grey texture that the file list gains nothing from.
verdict: Measured, the two panes are nearly the same: both Organizers are #EAEBEB, both Lists #FCFCFC, the divider #CBCCCC on both, names #191919 and excerpts #999999 on both, rows 136 device px apart, and a 6 px accent bar at x=276–281 with no row fill (#36BFFA on A, #00BFFF on B). B's List is one flat sheet with plain outline icons, so a writer's eye goes straight to the names and first lines. A lays shaded headers and shaded paper icons over the same grid, which is fussier without being clearer. B's Sort pill is too faint to read as a button, and that is the only thing holding the margin to slight.

states.name: search
states.gap: B's row rules run from x=340 to about x=700, and A's stop at about x=692. The rules overshoot the right edge of the date column, which ends at about x=696 in B and x=686 in A. That leaves a right gutter of about 20 px against A's 28 px, so the list looks jammed against the window edge. The field's icon is also a magnifier where A uses a filter glyph.
states.gapTheirs: The first file row starts 190 px down A's list, against 150 px in B. That is 40 device px of toolbar (a back button, a location title with a cloud icon, and a +/chevron button cluster of about 160×70 px) sitting above the documents before the Sort pill. A also shows a '.txt' row whose excerpt has no visible 'sea' in it, which adds a result that means nothing at a glance.
states.verdict: The two panes are almost the same measured list: rows 136 px apart, a 6 px accent bar at #00BFFF against A's #36BFFA, grounds of #EAEBEB and #FCFCFC, and excerpts and dates both at grey 153. A spends an extra 40 px of toolbar before any document shows, and its list includes a hit you can't see matching. B trims its right margin too tight, so rules and dates crowd the edge by 8–10 px. A writer scanning search results would get to the manuscript faster in B, but only just.

The Sort pill's darkest text is 117 in A and 118 in B, which is identical in practice.
The list title's darkest pixel is 84 in A and 74 in B. B's 'library' is set bold and larger, centred with no icon.
The Filter field sits at the foot in both, with the same blue focus ring and clear button. A uses a filter glyph and B a magnifier.
B's file icon is a flat outline page. A's is a greyed thumbnail-style page.
B's Organizer empty-state text for Pinned wraps to 3 lines at about 34 px pitch, a match for A's Favorites text.
